title: Shard clock skew causing stepwise per-model cost and quota anomalies
creator: Amira Johnson
description: Symptom: Several customers reported sudden stepwise jumps in per-model daily cost and quota usage charts that appear only after the nightly compaction window. These spikes are not present in raw token-event streams and are not correlated with increased request rate.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-01: Data team alerted via PagerDuty after observing >30% step increases in model A cost chart during compaction. 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-05: Initial triage showed discrepancies between raw ingest events and console aggregates. 2026-03-08: Hypothesis formed around shard-local timestamps and compaction merging. 2026-03-11: Repro script validated attribute attribution flip when shard clocks drift >5s. 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation deployed to delay compaction merge until alias refresh completes.
steps_to_reproduce: Seed two ingestion shards with overlapping events for the same model alias where shard A clock is ahead by 7s and shard B is behind by 4s.
Trigger the nightly compaction job that merges prefix/kv cache and ingested usage events into the daily aggregator.

Observe the per-model console chart and per-model quota consumption: counts from the ahead shard are merged after the alias-mapping refresh, causing attribution into a later bucket and creating an apparent step increase at compaction time.
Compare against raw event stream logs to confirm events are present earlier than the displayed jump.
investigation_notes: Root cause appears to be twofold: 1) shard-local ingestion timestamps are used downstream for bucketing instead of normalized event_time, and 2) alias mapping cache TTL can expire between ingest and compaction causing events to be reattributed to fallback model ids during merge.

When compaction merges out-of-order events, our aggregator currently applies a 'merge-winner' logic that prefers the later shard batch's attribution metadata, effectively reassigning previously credited tokens to a different bucket.

Rate-limit events are recorded as separate telemetry with a different ingestion path. Some rate-limit replays were merged incorrectly and counted as consumed tokens instead of blocked attempts, inflating cost charts.
Observed clock skew across shards of up to 9s in the affected region; drift correlates with magnitude of chart step.
Sampling a small backfill replay replicated the step effect locally, confirming logic in aggregator during compaction is the trigger rather than the original ingestion pipeline.
temporary_mitigation: Deployed a compaction hold for affected region to process alias refresh prior to merge (temporary, adds ~30s to compaction).
Adjusted console UI to flag charts with recent compaction merges and show 'data under reconciliation' tooltip to reduce customer confusion.
Added monitoring alert for compaction merge reattribution rate >0.5% between windows.
proposed_solution: 1) Normalize event_time during ingest and preserve original event_time downstream; ensure aggregator buckets by normalized event_time, not shard_local_time.

2) Strengthen alias-mapping resolution at compaction time: resolve alias mapping deterministically using the alias_version recorded at original ingest when available; fallback to earliest consistent mapping otherwise.
3) Change compaction merge logic to be idempotent with respect to attribution metadata: if attribution changes during merge, emit a reconciliation delta event rather than silently reassigning tokens.
4) Add unit tests and integration test that simulate shard-clock-skew and alias TTL expiry to prevent regressions.
5) Roll out fixes behind feature flag and run a canary on non-critical orgs for 48 hours before full rollout.
qa_criteria: No stepwise jumps in per-model daily cost charts after compaction in canary orgs for 48 hours.
Aggregated console values match raw event stream counts within 0.05% for last 7 days in canary orgs.
Reconciliation delta events are generated and visible in observability for any changed attributions post-merge.
Load test with synthetic clock skew up to 15s shows no incorrect reattribution.
rollback_plan: Revert compaction-related changes via feature flag toggles if we detect a >0.2% increase in net billed tokens during canary.
Re-enable temporary compaction hold and UI flag if rollback occurs and open an incident to triage.

2026-03-08 — Priya Shah (Observability): Added compaction reattribution alert and dashboard panel to track delta events; alert fired twice overnight in prod region-1.

Observability panels report reconciliation deltas and show zero silent reattributions during canary.
Post-release automated backfill of any reconciliation deltas for affected time ranges is scheduled and validated.
Documentation updated: compaction behavior, alias mapping guarantees, and FAQ entry for customers.
